Hi Roman, Acme Corp has approved the proposed CRM Migration timeline. Please share the final implementation plan and next steps. Regards, Alice Johnson
Hi Roman, TechNova would like a revised commercial proposal for the AI Analytics Platform. Please include the updated pricing and licensing assumptions. Regards, David Miller
Hi Brock, We reviewed the Data Warehouse migration plan. Please confirm the migration phases, validation process, and target completion date. Regards, Sophia Moore
Hi Brock, SecureNet needs additional documentation around security controls before we can proceed with the Security Platform proposal. Regards, Daniel Thomas
Hi Steve, PayFlow would like to discuss revised payment terms and transaction-volume pricing for the Payment Gateway. Regards, Charlotte Lee
Hi Steve, TravelEase confirms the final Mobile App scope. We are ready to proceed with the agreed implementation plan. Regards, Amelia Hall
Hi Kurt, Figma is reviewing the enterprise pricing for the Figma Enterprise project. Please send the final pricing breakdown and licensing details. Regards, Harper Young
Hi Kurt, After reviewing the proposal, Acme Corp has decided not to proceed with the Marketing Automation project at this time. Regards, Evelyn Wright
Hi John, PeopleFirst would like to schedule a demonstration of the AI Support Platform, especially the automation and escalation capabilities. Regards, Grace Hill
Hi John, DataSphere needs additional technical architecture details for the Enterprise Data Platform before the next review. Regards, Chloe Mitchell

Roman: Hi Alice, thanks for joining. I wanted to use this session to lock down the migration scope and timeline. Alice Johnson: Sure. From our side the biggest priority is moving the customer records without disrupting the sales team's daily work. Mark Wilson: And we need the reporting dashboards to keep working during the transition. We don't want a gap in reporting. Roman: Understood. We can run the old and new systems in parallel for the first two weeks. That gives us a rollback option. Alice Johnson: That works. What do you need from our team before the first migration? Roman: A cleaned export of the customer data and one person from your team to validate the migrated records. Mark Wilson: I can own the validation. We also have some duplicate records that should probably be cleaned before migration. Roman: Good point. We'll include a duplicate check in the preparation phase. Alice Johnson: Then I'm comfortable with the timeline you sent yesterday. Roman: Great. I'll send the final implementation plan and we'll start with the data preparation next Monday.

Roman: Thanks for making time. Today I'd like to get more specific about the analytics use cases and the commercial expectations. David Miller: The main thing we want is a dashboard that shows revenue, customer activity, and pipeline movement in one place. Emily Davis: We also need filters by region and product. Our current reports are too manual. Roman: That's all supported. The question is volume. How many users do you expect initially? David Miller: Around 120 users, with maybe another 80 over the next year. Roman: Okay. That changes the pricing tier slightly. I can prepare a revised proposal based on 120 users and projected growth. Emily Davis: Please also separate implementation from the recurring license. Procurement needs those as separate line items. Roman: Absolutely. I'll make that distinction clear. David Miller: If the revised pricing is reasonable, we should be able to move to the commercial review. Roman: I'll send the revised proposal tomorrow and we can review it in the next meeting.

Brock: Let's start with the migration scope. Sophia, can you walk us through the current data sources? Sophia Moore: We have the CRM, billing system, support platform, and two legacy databases. Michael Taylor: The legacy databases are the difficult part. Their schemas are inconsistent and there are a lot of historical records. Brock: How much history do you actually need in the new warehouse? Sophia Moore: Seven years for finance and three years for operational reporting. Brock: That is manageable. We'll archive the older operational data rather than loading all of it into the active warehouse. Michael Taylor: What about validation? We need confidence that the totals match the source systems. Brock: We'll create reconciliation checks for record counts and key financial totals at every migration stage. Sophia Moore: Good. Can you put those checks into the implementation plan? Brock: Yes. I'll add them along with the migration phases and target dates.

Brock: Daniel, before we talk about the final proposal, I want to understand the security concerns you raised in email. Daniel Thomas: The main issue is data isolation. We need confirmation that one customer can never access another customer's data. Olivia Martin: We also need audit logs for administrative actions and a documented retention policy. Brock: Both are supported. We can provide tenant-level isolation and immutable audit records. Daniel Thomas: We need that in writing. Our security team won't approve the purchase based on a verbal confirmation. Brock: That's fair. I'll send the architecture and security documentation. Olivia Martin: There's also a pricing concern. The current proposal is above the budget we approved. Brock: Is the budget fixed, or is there flexibility if we reduce the initial scope? Daniel Thomas: The budget is effectively fixed for this year. Brock: Understood. I'll see what we can do, but I don't want to promise a number before checking internally. Daniel Thomas: Then let's pause the commercial decision until we have the security documents and a revised option. Brock: Agreed. I'll send the documentation first and follow up with a revised proposal.

Brock: Thanks everyone. I want to use this meeting for the final review before we move the portal into implementation. William Jackson: The latest build looks good. The login and account-management flows are working as expected. Emma White: We tested the support workflow too. The only change we requested was adding a confirmation message after submitting a request. Brock: That can be included without changing the delivery date. William Jackson: What about the launch process? Brock: We'll do a controlled rollout first, monitor errors for 24 hours, and then open it to all users. Emma White: That sounds reasonable. Do you need anything else from us? Brock: Just the final list of production users and the support escalation contacts. William Jackson: We'll send those today. Brock: Perfect. Once we have those, I'll mark the project ready for implementation.

Steve: Charlotte, I'd like to focus today on transaction volume and the commercial terms. Charlotte Lee: Our expected volume is around 1.5 million transactions per month initially. Henry Lewis: And we'd like the pricing to step down as volume increases. Steve: We can structure volume-based pricing. I need to confirm the exact thresholds internally. Charlotte Lee: Our finance team also wants net-45 payment terms. Steve: Our standard is net-30, but I can take net-45 back for approval. Henry Lewis: If both of those are workable, the technical side is already in good shape. Steve: That's helpful. I'll separate the pricing tiers and payment terms in the revised proposal. Charlotte Lee: Good. Let's target the commercial review for next week. Steve: Agreed. I'll send the updated proposal before then.

Steve: Thanks for joining. Today is the final scope review for the mobile application. Amelia Hall: We reviewed the latest build and the core booking flow is correct. Alexander Walker: We also tested notifications. There was one issue with delayed push notifications, but it appears fixed. Steve: Good. Are there any remaining blockers from your side? Amelia Hall: No blockers. We'd like analytics events for booking, cancellation, and payment confirmation. Steve: Those events are already in the implementation plan. Alexander Walker: What is the deployment sequence? Steve: We'll deploy to the internal test group first, then a small percentage of production users, and expand after monitoring. Amelia Hall: That works for us. Steve: Great. I'll mark the scope as approved and send the deployment checklist.

Kurt: Harper, thanks for joining. I want to close the remaining questions around enterprise licensing. Harper Young: The functionality looks right. The open question is the annual price at our expected user count. Matthew Allen: We also need the enterprise security terms reviewed by our legal team. Kurt: We can provide the security documentation today. For pricing, what user count should I use for the final proposal? Harper Young: Around 600 users initially, with a possibility of 900 by the end of the year. Kurt: Okay. I'll price the initial commitment at 600 and include the expansion tier separately. Matthew Allen: That would help procurement compare the options. Kurt: I'll also include the implementation and support costs as separate line items. Harper Young: Good. If the numbers are within our range, we can move to legal review. Kurt: I'll send the final commercial proposal tomorrow.

Kurt: Evelyn, I'd like to understand the decision before we close the opportunity. Evelyn Wright: The product itself was well received. The issue is the expected return compared with the implementation cost. Ethan King: We ran the numbers again after the proposal. We don't think the first-year savings justify the investment. Kurt: Would reducing the initial scope change that calculation? Evelyn Wright: Possibly, but we'd still have the internal change-management cost. Kurt: Understood. If we proposed a smaller pilot, would that be something you'd consider? Evelyn Wright: Not right now. We have another initiative competing for the same budget. Ethan King: We'd rather revisit this next planning cycle. Kurt: That's clear. I'll record the opportunity as closed and note that budget allocation and ROI were the main reasons. Evelyn Wright: That accurately reflects our decision.

John: Grace, I'll start with a quick overview and then we can focus on the workflows that matter to PeopleFirst. Grace Hill: The biggest issue for us is repetitive HR support questions. Employees ask the same things constantly. Logan Nelson: We'd like the assistant to answer those questions but escalate anything involving sensitive employee information. John: That's a good fit. We can define escalation rules based on topic and confidence. Grace Hill: Can it also surface the source of the answer? Our HR team needs to verify policy responses. John: Yes. We can include the source document with each response. Logan Nelson: What about integration with our existing ticketing system? John: We have an API integration for that. Tickets can be created automatically when the assistant escalates a case. Grace Hill: That covers our main requirements. We'd like a technical demo next. John: I'll schedule the demo and include the ticketing and escalation workflows.
